cases: PyInstaller onedir package launches offline on supported Windows x64 with Python-runtime bundle and no installed Node requirement.
Inno per-user install completes without elevation, firewall rule or Windows service.
Install root and separate instance root resolve under governed LocalAppData locations.
Owner-appropriate ACL checks reject unsafe security/runtime/diagnostic path redirection or reparse target.
Packaged runtime binds only 127.0.0.1 using exclusive socket semantics.
Tray open/start/stop controls operate only on freshly verified SOMA instance identity.
Closing every browser window leaves authoritative host running.
Source deployment start/stop launchers use the same trusted-control protocol as packaged tray.
Release dependency manifest includes exact SQLCipher/Argon2/cryptography/PyInstaller/Inno selections and hashes where applicable.
Package scan finds no customer data, databases, logs, backups, workbooks, PST/OST/MSG, credentials or runtime registry.
Upgrade preserves instance root and invokes only accepted LLD-01 migration path after security initialization.
Upgrade failure preserves prior data and yields sanitized bounded diagnostics.
Uninstall stops only a currently reverified SOMA run, never a reused PID/port process.
Default uninstall preserves database, DPAPI envelopes, managed backups and diagnostics.
Release candidate smoke matrix proves startup/login/backup/restore/browser/tray on representative Windows 10/11 and Python 3.13/3.14 compatibility lines.
A complete .somabackupset directory copied intact to another supported installation is recognized as one portable recovery deliverable; selecting payload.somabackup alone is rejected.
expected: Packaging preserves offline, local-only, data-preserving and exact-runtime trust guarantees.
